decisions.old_behaviour: SET table silently removes exact duplicate rows. Seeded staging has 300 rows, 250 distinct; source has 250. runner.py enforces UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
decisions.new_behaviour: Plain Snowflake table keeps all 300 rows. No DISTINCT or owner-approved SET decision has been added.
decisions.question: Should exact duplicate storage usage be discarded or retained for charging? Choose distinct or keep_all explicitly; warehouse/dbt/macros/set_table_semantics.sql already requires that decision.

decisions.old_behaviour: ROW_NUMBER partitions by DOCUMENT_ID and sorts only VERSION_TS DESC. Fifty seeded documents have two distinct versions at the same latest timestamp; winner is unspecified.
decisions.new_behaviour: Candidate keeps the same incomplete ordering. A local matching winner does not establish deterministic parity across engines.
decisions.question: Which version wins equal latest timestamps? No VERSION_NO/ID tie breaker will be invented.

decisions.old_behaviour: XML lookup policy is Use First Value. For multiple role grants per USER_ID the runner selects the first cached match.
decisions.new_behaviour: Existing pc_content__doc_share joins every matching role. The local merge guard rejects duplicate SHARE_IDs instead of choosing a role. Seeded 20-row ROLE_GRANT has unique USER_IDs, so this is a synthetic error-case difference, not an observed seeded mismatch.
decisions.question: Which role wins for users with multiple grants? Preserve first cached match or choose an explicit role precedence? Existing dbt model is unchanged.

collab_session_sessionize.query: WITH previous_events AS (SELECT USER_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, EVENT_AT, LAG(EVENT_AT) OVER (PARTITION BY USER_ID, DOCUMENT_ID ORDER BY EVENT_AT) AS PREVIOUS_EVENT_AT FROM SPARK_INPUT.COLLAB_SESSION), session_boundaries AS (SELECT USER_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, EVENT_AT, CASE WHEN PREVIOUS_EVENT_AT IS NULL OR DATE_DIFF('MICROSECOND', PREVIOUS_EVENT_AT, EVENT_AT) > 1800000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS NEW_SESSION FROM previous_events), numbered_events AS (SELECT USER_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, EVENT_AT, SUM(NEW_SESSION) OVER (PARTITION BY USER_ID, DOCUMENT_ID ORDER BY EVENT_AT range BETWEEN UNBOUNDED preceding AND CURRENT ROW) AS SESSION_NUMBER FROM session_boundaries) SELECT USER_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, SESSION_NUMBER, MIN(EVENT_AT) AS START_AT, MAX(EVENT_AT) AS END_AT FROM numbered_events GROUP BY USER_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, SESSION_NUMBER

security_alert_anomaly.query: WITH alerts AS (SELECT SECURITY_ALERT_ID AS ALERT_ID, USER_ID, CAST(SCORE AS DOUBLE) AS SCORE FROM SPARK_INPUT.SECURITY_ALERT), moments AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS N, CAST(COALESCE(SUM(SCORE), 0) AS DOUBLE) AS TOTAL, CAST(COALESCE(SUM(SCORE * SCORE), 0) AS DOUBLE) AS SQUARES FROM alerts), distribution AS (SELECT TOTAL / GREATEST(N, 1) AS MEAN, SQRT(GREATEST(SQUARES / GREATEST(N, 1) - POWER(TOTAL / GREATEST(N, 1), 2), 0)) AS SD FROM moments) SELECT a.ALERT_ID, a.USER_ID, a.SCORE, (a.SCORE - d.MEAN) / CASE WHEN d.SD = 0 THEN 1 ELSE d.SD END AS Z_SCORE FROM alerts AS a CROSS JOIN distribution AS d
